title: Processing RF Work: Pick Into Container
titles: Processing RF Work: Pick Into Container

children:
This type of RF processing involves users picking product directly into 
 shipping containers (or a tote). When you pick directly into a 
 container, the system will perform the packing action as part of the picking 
 process (the user will be able to 
 assign the picked item and quantity to a specific container ID). Until this 
 container is closed, any other items belonging the same shipment may be 
 added to this container. When picking into a tote, the user can group 
 products on the same shipment together. This picking action is a derivative 
 of user/system-directed work, so please see the
section for details not covered explicitly in this section.

P&D Locations: When picking into final 
 shipping containers from a pickup-and-dropoff location, the system will 
 never actually display the P&D location to the user. Since there could 
 be multiple items in the container, the system would not know which item/location 
 to get the correct P&D location from.

Picking Into Totes: The procedures 
 outlined below are the same when picking directly into a tote. However, 
 the system will not ask for a container type, or create a shipping container. You will need to indicate on your work profile that you want to pick into totes (as opposed to shipping containers).

Creating Containers in the Wave: The following scenario is not supported: Creating containers during the wave (the work generated from allocation requests), and then executing the pick/putaway into a shipping container via RF, as the system would have no way to link the work from the allocation requests to the existing container that you would be picking into.
You can pick  multiple shipment details going to different putaway locations into a single tote.

1. Log on to your RF Device and select the Work function. The system will 
 display the Work Profile Selection Screen.

2. If you have a 
 default work profile defined for your user profile, the system 
 will automatically choose this profile and direct you to the appropriate 
 work screen. Otherwise, you will need to manually 
 choose a work profile.
3. Scan the work initiation value, and press OK:
You can only scan the work unit if it is the only thing you have available. You will have the opportunity to scan the container ID you are picking into on the Pick Confirmation screen.
You can also scan both of these values if they are available at the time of work initiation.

4. The system will display the first work instruction of the assigned work unit in the Pick Confirmation 
 screen.
5. Enter the quantity that you want to pick.
6. You may have to verify the following values (if your work special handling record is configured to do so):

7. You may choose to override certain pick values (if your work special handling record is configured to do so). This is done by entering one of the following values in an edit box next to the appropriate field on the Pick Confirmation Screen. Note that you can also configure the system in work special handling to warn the user an override is about to occur (after they press OK to confirm the pick):
8. Press one of the following picking buttons:

9. The system will 
 display the Container Type Screen. On this screen, you can indicate 
 the type of shipping container you want to pick the item quantity into. The container types can be authorized by company and warehouse.
10. The system will then display the Putaway Confirmation screen, if automatic putaway is not configured on your work profile. Press one of the following putaway buttons:

        7. You may choose to override certain pick values (if your work special handling record is configured to do so).
